page.description: Haiku editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: An open-source reimplementation of BeOS: its own kernel and userland, fast boot, and a package manager. One image boots live and installs.
pros: A complete desktop system that boots in seconds.
BeOS binary compatibility keeps old BeOS applications running.
One image works as a live session and as the installer.
Packages come from Haiku's own repositories with pkgman.
cons: Still a beta: the project labels R1/beta6 as a test release.
Not Linux and not BSD: Linux drivers and tools do not apply.
A smaller application and hardware support base than the mainstream systems.
The Commons screenshot shows an older Haiku desktop.
page.previewNote: A stock screenshot of the Haiku desktop with Tracker, from Wikimedia Commons. It is not the R1/beta6 image and not a ROMinit recording: no image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted for this page.

page.status: One image: the x86_64 anyboot ISO, which boots live and installs from the same session. Writing the stick erases it; the installer then writes to the partition or disk you choose.
